meta.name: Consumer GPU Model Card
meta.sample_label: Curated sample of well-known public GPUs and quantized models. Not a complete list, not a leaderboard, and not a set of measurements taken for this project.
meta.disclaimer: Model VRAM, disk, and system RAM figures are rounded estimates. This repository did not run tokens-per-second benchmarks. GPU memory sizes are vendor-published specs, listed so you can identify the card.
meta.estimate_basis: Estimate basis: a typical public GGUF file size for that quant, plus a few GB for the runtime and the KV cache at roughly 4k–8k tokens. Numbers are rounded on purpose.
meta.weights_note: This site does not host weights. Open the public model card, then choose a GGUF-style quant whose filename matches the row (for example Q4_K_M) from a publisher you trust. Some model cards ask you to accept a license.

fit_rule.context_note: Estimate assumes a short context, roughly 4k–8k tokens. Longer chats grow the KV cache and can move a row from likely to tight or to partial offload.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 4060 8GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the 8GB retail card. Confirm the exact board before buying.
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 3B Q4 is the comfortable start on 8GB. A 7B or 8B Q4 row is often tight at short context.
Estimate: 8B Q8 and 12B-class Q4 usually need a smaller quant or partial offload.
Estimate: 16GB system RAM is a practical first-build floor. 32GB is easier if you offload layers.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 3060 12GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the 12GB retail card. An 8GB RTX 3060 also exists; match the GB on the box.
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you. Ampere cards are still common on the used market.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 7B–9B Q4/Q5 is the comfortable band. 8B Q8 and 12B–14B Q4 are often tight.
Estimate: 27B and 32B Q4 weights generally mean partial CPU offload on 12GB.
Estimate: 32GB system RAM is a sensible target when you use a 12GB card and sometimes offload.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 4070 12GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the 12GB RTX 4070. Fit estimates follow capacity, not shader count.
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: same 12GB capacity band as a 3060 12GB. Extra GPU speed does not raise the VRAM ceiling.
Estimate: 7B–9B Q4/Q5 is comfortable. 14B Q4 is often tight once context and the desktop take space.
Estimate: plan about 32GB system RAM if you want room to offload a larger quant.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 5070 12GB
gpus.spec_note: NVIDIA's GeForce compare table lists 12 GB GDDR7 and a 192-bit interface for the RTX 5070 (published spec).
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 12GB class. Newer memory generations do not, by themselves, fit a larger weight file.
Estimate: 7B–9B Q4/Q5 is the comfortable starter band. 14B Q4 is often tight.
Estimate: 32GB system RAM pairs more calmly with a 12GB card than 16GB does.

gpus.name: Intel Arc B580 12GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the Arc B580 12GB retail card. Confirm on Intel's product page.
gpus.runtime_note: CUDA builds do not drive this card. Look at llama.cpp Vulkan or SYCL builds.
capacity_notes: Estimate: capacity class matches other 12GB cards. Software support is the part to check first.
Estimate: 7B–9B Q4/Q5 is the comfortable band if your runtime actually uses the GPU.
Estimate: keep about 32GB system RAM so a Vulkan or SYCL build still has room to offload.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 4060 Ti 16GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the 16GB RTX 4060 Ti. An 8GB variant of the same name exists.
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 7B–14B Q4/Q5 is a comfortable starting band at short context.
Estimate: 27B–32B Q4 is commonly a partial offload on 16GB, not a roomy full-GPU fit.
Estimate: the narrow memory bus is a published spec detail. This card still sorts models by the 16GB capacity.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB
gpus.spec_note: NVIDIA's GeForce compare table lists an RTX 5060 Ti in 16 GB and 8 GB GDDR7 configs. This row is the 16GB card.
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: pick the 16GB board on purpose. The 8GB RTX 5060 Ti is a different capacity class.
Estimate: 7B–14B Q4/Q5 is the comfortable short-context band.
Estimate: 32B Q4 weights generally spill into partial offload on 16GB.

gpus.name: Radeon RX 7800 XT 16GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the RX 7800 XT (16 GB GDDR6). Confirm on AMD's product page.
gpus.runtime_note: CUDA builds do not drive this card. Look at llama.cpp Vulkan or ROCm builds.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 16GB class, same capacity band as a 16GB GeForce, with a different software path.
Estimate: 7B–14B Q4/Q5 is a comfortable starting band at short context.
Estimate: budget about 32GB system RAM if you plan to offload, plus tens of GB of disk for GGUF files.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 4070 Ti Super 16GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the RTX 4070 Ti Super 16GB. The earlier 4070 Ti is a 12GB card.
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 16GB class. Do not confuse it with the 12GB RTX 4070 Ti.
Estimate: 7B–14B Q4/Q5 fits the comfortable short-context band.
Estimate: 27B–32B Q4 is commonly tight or a partial offload.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 4080 16GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the 16GB RTX 4080 / 4080 Super class.
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: faster than a 4060 Ti 16GB, same 16GB capacity ceiling for weights.
Estimate: 7B–14B Q4/Q5 is the comfortable short-context band.
Estimate: 70B Q4 weights stay well above a 16GB card.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 5080 16GB
gpus.spec_note: NVIDIA's GeForce compare table lists 16 GB GDDR7 and a 256-bit interface for the RTX 5080 (published spec).
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 7B–14B Q4/Q5 is a comfortable starting band at short context.
Estimate: 27B–32B Q4 is commonly a partial offload on 16GB, not a roomy full-GPU fit.
Estimate: pair the card with about 32GB system RAM if you offload, and leave 20–40GB of disk free for a few GGUF files.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 4090 24GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the RTX 4090 (24 GB GDDR6X).
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 14B–32B Q4 is the interesting band. 32B Q4 is often tight once context grows.
Estimate: 70B Q4 still wants partial offload or a smaller quant on 24GB.
Estimate: 64GB system RAM is the calmer partner if you experiment with 70B-class splits.

gpus.name: Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24GB
gpus.spec_note: Widely published vendor memory config for the RX 7900 XTX (24 GB GDDR6). Confirm on AMD's product page.
gpus.runtime_note: CUDA builds do not drive this card. Look at llama.cpp Vulkan or ROCm builds.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 24GB capacity class, similar weight ceiling to a 24GB GeForce, different runtime.
Estimate: 32B Q4 is often tight at short context. 70B Q4 is a partial-offload project.
Estimate: 64GB system RAM gives you room when a split model lands in CPU memory.

gpus.name: GeForce RTX 5090 32GB
gpus.spec_note: NVIDIA's GeForce compare table lists 32 GB GDDR7 and a 512-bit interface for the RTX 5090 (published spec).
gpus.runtime_note: Usual hobby path: llama.cpp built with CUDA, or a desktop app that runs GGUF for you.
capacity_notes: Estimate: 32B Q4 often fits with headroom at short context.
Estimate: 70B Q4 is still usually a partial offload on 32GB.
Estimate: 64GB system RAM is the comfortable partner for 70B-class experiments.

models.name: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct
models.note: Small instruct model. A common first download when VRAM is tight.

models.name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
models.note: Widely used general instruct GGUF. Q4_K_M is the usual hobbyist starting quant.

models.name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
models.note: Same 8B model at a higher-bit quant. Heavier file, chosen when the card has spare VRAM.

models.name: Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3
models.note: Older, still common 7B baseline. Q5_K_M is a popular middle quant.

models.name: Qwen2.5 7B Instruct
models.note: Strong small general model in the public Qwen2.5 family.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B Instruct
models.note: Code-leaning 7B. Same rough weight class as the general 7B Q4.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B
models.note: Small reasoning-style distill. Similar weight class to other 7B Q4 files.

models.name: Gemma 2 9B Instruct
models.note: Public Gemma 2 9B instruct model. Slightly heavier than an 8B Q4.

models.name: Mistral Nemo 12B Instruct
models.note: 12B instruct model. A step up in size from the 7B and 8B rows.

models.name: Phi-4
models.note: Microsoft Phi-4, a public 14B-class model. Q4_K_M is the hobbyist starting quant.

models.name: Qwen2.5 14B Instruct
models.note: Mid-size Qwen2.5. Often the largest comfortable Q4 on a 16GB card at short context.

models.name: Gemma 2 27B Instruct
models.note: Large Gemma 2. The Q4 file itself sits in the mid-teens of GB.

models.name: Qwen2.5 32B Instruct
models.note: 32B general instruct. A 24GB card is the first class where Q4 is even plausible.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B
models.note: Larger reasoning-style distill. Weight class similar to other 32B Q4 files.

models.name: Qwen2.5 72B Instruct
models.note: 72B at a more aggressive Q3 quant. Still a very large file.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct
models.note: 70B instruct. Treat a full-GPU fit as a high-VRAM problem.
